rows.note: Launch plan storage, billed per GB-month with no included allowance. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: Neon publishes Free, Launch and Scale; Launch and Scale are both 'Pay for what you use' with 'no monthly minimum' and the same $0.35/GB-month storage rate, so no cheaper plan can win these workloads.
Launch plan public network transfer (egress): 500 GB per project included, then $0.10/GB.
Pro plan base subscription: 'From $25/month' for the first project (includes $10/mo compute credit covering one Micro instance).

Pro plan disk size: 8 GB included per project, then $0.125 per GB. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: the Free plan enters read-only mode above 500 MB, so Pro is the only plan that is both capacity-capable and cheaper than Team.
Pro plan egress: 250 GB included, then $0.09 per GB.
PlanetScale Postgres HA (3-node: 1 primary + 2 replicas) cluster fee for the PS-80 arm64 SKU (1 vCPU, 8 GiB memory) in AWS us-east-1, from the official pricing table.

Postgres HA network-attached storage: first 10 GB free, then billed per GB beyond that; rate derived exactly from the live pricing calculator's computed total (delta of $375 for +1000 GB, i.e. $0.375/GB, independent of cluster SKU size).
Postgres HA egress bandwidth: '100 GB of egress bandwidth is included. Additional usage: $0.06/GB.'

PlanetScale Postgres EBS single node (non-HA), the cheapest paid Postgres cluster: 'PS-5 / 1/16 vCPU / 512 MB memory / 10 GB storage / $5 / Includes 1 node' in the AWS us-east-1 calculator, matching the published SKU table ('Postgres EBS non-HA (single node)': PS-5 x86-64 and PS-5 arm64 both $5). Calculator's estimated monthly total at the default 10 GB storage and 10 GB egress is $5.

Postgres EBS network-attached storage on a single node: 'the first 10 GB is free, with per-GB pricing beyond that'. Rate derived exactly from the live calculator's estimated monthly total, holding egress at its 10 GB included level: 1010 GB storage gives $130 against a $5 base, i.e. $125 for 1000 GB beyond the included 10 GB = $0.125/GB. One third of the $0.375/GB HA rate, which provisions the volume on all three nodes.

Single-node PS-5 egress bandwidth: '10 GB of egress bandwidth is included. Additional usage: $0.06 / GB.' The included allowance is SKU-specific and lower than the HA cluster's 100 GB. Confirmed against the calculator total: 1010 GB egress gives $65 against a $5 base, i.e. $60 for 1000 GB = $0.06/GB.
Entry PostgreSQL plan at $15.15/month; the base tier includes a 10 GiB to 30 GiB storage range. attributes.storage_gib records the floor of that range, 10 GiB, not the full range.
Storage expansion beyond the plan's included 10 GiB, quoted as $0.215/GiB/mo and sold in 10 GiB increments.
Essential 1 plan at $9/month including 10 GB of storage; Essential tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '10 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (9.31).
Essential 0 plan at $5/month including 1 GB of storage; Essential tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '1 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (0.93).
Essential 2 plan at $20/month including 32 GB of storage; Essential tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '32 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (29.8).

Standard 0 plan at $50/month including 64 GB of storage and 4 GB of memory; Standard tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '64 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (59.6).

Standard 2 plan at $200/month including 256 GB of storage and 8 GB of memory; Standard tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '256 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (238.42).

Standard 3 plan at $400/month including 512 GB of storage and 15 GB of memory; Standard tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '512 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (476.84).

Premium 2 plan at $350/month including 256 GB of storage and 8 GB of memory; Premium tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge. Vendor publishes '256 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (238.42).
Developer plan base fee, the cheapest paid tier: 'Developer / $4.99/month'.
Developer plan storage: 'Storage ... 9GB / + $0.75 / GB'. Page states 'GB' with no GiB/binary clarification.

Pay as You Go storage: 'For each database, the first 1GB is free. Beyond that, storage is charged at $0.25 per GB of total storage.' No fixed monthly fee exists for this plan, so no plan_base_month row is recorded.
Pay as You Go bandwidth: 'For pay-as-you-go, monthly bandwidth is free up to 200GB. Beyond that, we charge $0.03 per additional GB.'

M10 Dedicated cluster tier card: '$0.08/hour ... Starts at $56.94/month', confirmed with Storage 10 GB / RAM 2 GB / vCPUs 2 bundled at this tier (cross-checked against the Dedicated Cluster storage-range modal showing M10: 10-128 GB). $56.94/month is a derived monthly floor from the hourly rate, not a native flat monthly SKU, hence medium confidence. Storage-overage and egress rates are NOT recorded: MongoDB's own docs give no flat per-GB figure for either (storage overage docs say only 'charges for the full amount' with no rate; data-transfer docs give 'Out to Internet: $0.09 to $0.16' per GB as a range, confirmed live on https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs/). Lineup checked 2026-08-30: Free (0.5 GB) and Flex (5 GB hard cap) cannot hold either workload's data, so they are excluded by capacity rather than price. Among tiers that can, M10 is the cheapest.

Performance tier card: 'Storage priced at $0.177 / GB-month', metered from actual usage with no stated included allowance. Reached via a permanent redirect from https://www.timescale.com/pricing (Timescale has rebranded to Tiger Data / Tiger Cloud). plan_base_month is NOT recorded: the card's 'Compute starts at $30/month' is an hourly-metered floor for the smallest instance size, not a fixed recurring fee independent of usage, so entering it as plan_base_month would misrepresent it. egress_gib is NOT recorded: confirmed live via in-page text search that neither 'egress' nor 'transfer' appears anywhere on the page. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: every input that differs between Performance and Scale favours Performance, whose storage rate is lower, so no other tier can win.

Hobby-0 instance tier on AWS, the cheapest paid tier in the itemized table: 'Cores 2 | Memory .5GB | Price $9'. The page's own top banner separately advertises 'plans starting at $10/mo' -- a $1 discrepancy with this itemized table figure; $9 is recorded because it comes from the line-item table, not the marketing banner.

'Storage costs are $0.10 per GB. For example, 100 GB would be $10 per month.' No included allowance is stated on this page for any instance tier, so included_allowance is recorded as 0; medium confidence because a minimum provisioned volume size is common for block-storage-backed Postgres and was not explicitly ruled out or confirmed via the pricing calculator. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: the tier ladder only buys compute, and Hobby-0 at $9 is unambiguously the cheapest row in the itemized table; storage is a flat per-GB rate across all tiers.

Verbatim: 'Prices include infrastructure, backups, and data transfer.' Data transfer (egress) is bundled into every instance tier's price at no separate per-GB charge -- first-party evidence of a known zero, confirmed live on the page.

Startup-4 sub-tier -- the specific SKU behind the headline 'STARTUP starting from $75/month' -- confirmed via the 'View 7 plans' breakdown: 'Startup-4 | 1 | 2 | 4GB | 80 - 400 GB | $0.10 | $75'. attributes.storage_gib records the floor of the 80-400 GB range, matching this dataset's convention for a range-bundled plan (see DigitalOcean's row). Aiven's FAQ recommends Startup as the minimum plan for production workloads. Vendor publishes '80 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (74.51).

Verbatim: 'All networking cost included.' Confirmed via the plan comparison table that this feature is checked (available) for every paid PostgreSQL plan including Startup. First-party evidence of a known zero -- Aiven's pricing is explicitly 'all-inclusive', with no per-GB networking charge on any tier.

Startup-8 sub-tier, confirmed via the 'View 7 plans' breakdown: 'Startup-8 | 1 | 4 | 8GB | 175 - 875 GB | $0.20 | $145'. Recorded specifically because it is the cheapest Aiven PostgreSQL tier whose floor storage allotment meets or exceeds 100 GiB -- Startup-4's 80 GB floor falls short, so recording only Startup-4 would have produced a coverage gap against the plan-with-100gib-storage shape workload (the exact failure mode this dataset has previously published as a $150 error). Vendor publishes '175 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (162.98).
Verbatim: 'All networking cost included.' Same first-party bundled-zero evidence as the startup-4 row, recorded again under this plan name so the fact is visible against the startup-8 group too.

Starter plan base fee: 'Starter / $10/month'. This fee is a combined platform charge covering both Prisma Postgres and the separate Prisma Compute app-hosting product's included allowances; it is not possible to isolate a database-only portion, but this matches how Prisma itself bills (one bill, no split).
Starter plan Prisma Postgres storage: '10 GB storage, then $2.00 per GB' (comparison table: 'Storage included | 10 GB', 'Storage overage | $2.00 per GB').

Verbatim: 'Unlimited Prisma Postgres data transfer' listed under 'Every plan includes'; comparison table also shows 'Data transfer | Unlimited' across all plans. This is the database's own data transfer and is unlimited/free; it is distinct from the separate Prisma Compute product's metered 'Outbound bandwidth' ($0.025/GB), which is a different product line and not recorded here as database egress.

Business plan: '$129/month', comparison table 'Storage included | 100GB'. The page does not state whether GB is decimal or binary; recorded as decimal (100 x 10^9 bytes = 93.13 GiB), the conservative reading. Under a binary reading this plan would provide exactly 100 GiB.
Scaler plan base fee, quoted as '$24.92/month' with '24GB' storage included.
Scaler storage overage, quoted as '$0.50 / GB' beyond the 24GB included in the plan.
4 vCPU / 8 GiB plan at $122.10/month, storage range '140 GiB - 280 GiB'. DigitalOcean states GiB explicitly, so the 140 floor needs no unit conversion.
Storage expansion beyond this plan's 140 GiB floor, quoted as '$0.215/GiB/mo, 10 GiB increments'.

Fixed 500GB tier at '$1500/month'. Vendor publishes '500 GB'; recorded as decimal converted to GiB (500 x 10^9 / 2^30 = 465.66). The cheaper Fixed 100GB tier was not used for the shape workload: '100 GB' is 93.13 GiB decimal and would not clear a 100 GiB threshold.

General Purpose SSD (gp3) capacity, read live from the pricing table with the page's region selector at its default, 'US East (Ohio)': 'General Purpose SSD (gp3) - Storage $0.08/GB-month'. The page states elsewhere, as a footnote to its worked examples, '*on this page, GB = 1024^3 bytes*' -- i.e. AWS's GB here already means GiB, so no unit conversion is needed. Free performance baseline: 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s throughput included ('All gp3 volumes include a free baseline performance of 3,000 provisioned IOPS ... and 125 provisioned MB/s throughput'); IOPS/throughput beyond that are billed separately ($0.005/provisioned IOPS-month, $0.040/provisioned MB/s-month) and are NOT included in this capacity figure. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: AWS sells four SSD-class volume types (gp3, gp2, io1, io2) plus two HDD/archival types (st1, sc1) excluded per this dataset's SSD-only scope; gp3 is the cheapest SSD-class volume and wins this workload.

General Purpose SSD (gp2) capacity, same live table, same default region (US East, Ohio): 'General Purpose SSD (gp2) Volumes $0.10 per GB-month of provisioned storage'. IOPS/throughput are bundled into the price at no separate charge (no free-baseline-plus-metered-overage structure, unlike gp3). Recorded to complete AWS's SSD lineup per the multi-plan rule; more expensive than gp3, does not win this workload.

Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) capacity, same live table, same default region: 'Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) - Storage $0.125/GB-month'. Unlike gp3, io2 has no free IOPS baseline -- IOPS are billed separately and tiered ('$0.065/provisioned IOPS-month up to 32,000 IOPS ...') from the first provisioned IOPS, none included. Recorded to complete AWS's SSD lineup; more expensive than gp3, does not win this workload.

Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) capacity, same live table, same default region: 'Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) Volumes $0.125 per GB-month of provisioned storage AND $0.065 per provisioned IOPS-month' -- storage price identical to io2; io1 is AWS's earlier-generation Provisioned IOPS SSD line, still sold alongside io2. No free IOPS baseline, same as io2. Recorded to complete AWS's SSD lineup; more expensive than gp3, does not win this workload.

EBS Snapshots Storage Pricing, live table: 'Standard $0.05/GB-month'. Same page-wide 'GB = 1024^3 bytes' convention as volume pricing, so no conversion needed. Billed incrementally: 'For each incremental snapshot, only the changed part of your Amazon EBS volume is saved.' Restoring from Standard is free.

EBS Snapshots Storage Pricing, live table: 'Archive $0.0125/GB-month'. Cheaper than Standard tier but carries a 90-day minimum retention period and a retrieval fee ($0.03/GB) to restore -- verbatim: 'There is a 90-day minimum retention period for snapshots stored in EBS Snapshots Archive.' Restoring from Standard, by contrast, is free. Recorded as its own plan per the multi-plan rule; the retention/retrieval tradeoff is not reflected in this monthly figure -- see the snapshot-storage-100gib workload's caveats.

Balanced Persistent Disk provisioned space, read live from the Persistent Disk and Hyperdisk pricing table after switching the page's region selector from its default (Iowa, us-central1) to 'Northern Virginia (us-east4)', the closest us-east-numbered region GCP offers: 'Balanced provisioned space $0.11 / 1 gibibyte month' (native monthly figure shown directly by the table's Monthly/Hourly toggle, not derived from an hourly rate). Page-wide unit note: 'disk size ... calculated in JEDEC binary gigabytes (GB), or IEC gibibytes (GiB)' -- GCP's own 'GB' already means GiB. IOPS/throughput are bundled at no separate charge for Balanced PD: 'Standard, SSD, and balanced Persistent Disks are priced by the amount of provisioned space per disk ... I/O operations are included in the price for provisioned space.'

Hyperdisk Balanced provisioned space, same live table, same region (us-east4, Northern Virginia): 'Hyperdisk Balanced provisioned space $0.08 / 1 gibibyte month'. Unlike Balanced PD, Hyperdisk Balanced meters IOPS and throughput separately beyond a free baseline: 'Hyperdisk Balanced ... charge a monthly rate for the provisioned IOPS and provisioned throughput ... in excess of the baseline values of 3,000 IOPS and 140 MBps throughput.' This capacity figure assumes that included baseline and excludes IOPS/throughput bought beyond it (IOPS $0.005/IOPS-month, throughput $0.04/MBps-month from the same table, not priced in this workload). Cheapest of the two recorded GCP plans; wins this workload.

Standard snapshot storage, live table under the same us-east4 region selection: 'Standard snapshot storage $0.05 / 1 gibibyte month'. Billed incrementally: 'Standard snapshots only incur charges for the total size of the snapshots ... only the changed part ... is saved.'

Archive snapshot storage, same live table: 'Archive snapshot storage $0.019 / 1 gibibyte month'. Cheaper than Standard tier but archive retrieval costs extra ('Archive snapshot retrieval $0.019 / 1 gibibyte'). Recorded as its own plan per the multi-plan rule; wins this workload, and the retrieval tradeoff is not reflected in this monthly figure -- see the snapshot-storage-100gib workload's caveats.

Premium SSD v2 capacity, read live with the page's region selector explicitly set to 'us-east' (East US; on this visit the selector's own default was already East US, though earlier research on this page observed a default of East US 2 -- both are selectable and this row is for East US as directed): 'Disk Capacity GiBs $0.081/GiB'. Free performance baseline: 'Up to 3,000 IOPS at no additional cost, $0.0052/provisioned IOPS over 3,000 IOPS' and 'Up to 125 MB/s at no additional cost, $0.041/provisioned MB/s over 125 MB/s' -- this capacity figure assumes that baseline and excludes IOPS/throughput bought beyond it. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: Azure also sells Premium SSD (P-series) and Standard SSD (E-series), both fixed-size disk SKUs (e.g. P10 128GiB for a flat $19.71/month) rather than a continuous per-GiB rate -- a derived tier-price/tier-size rate would misrepresent how they're actually billed, so they are not recorded under this metric. Ultra Disk ($0.11972/GiB-month, also continuously priced) is excluded as a specialized, no-free-baseline tier Microsoft positions for 'data-intensive workloads such as SAP HANA' rather than general-purpose use. Standard HDD is excluded per this dataset's HDD rule. Premium SSD v2 is therefore the only plan recorded for this metric.

Incremental snapshot storage on Standard storage, live page prose, applies uniformly across Ultra Disk, Premium SSD v2, and Premium SSD source disks: 'They are charged at $0.05/GB per month for both Standard LRS and ZRS snapshot options of the storage occupied by the delta changes since the last snapshot.' The page states 'GB' without clarifying decimal vs. binary, unlike its Premium SSD v2/Ultra Disk capacity tables which explicitly say 'GiB' -- per this dataset's conservative-reading rule, recorded as-is (unconverted) with the ambiguity flagged, the same convention already used for Turso's ambiguous '$0.75/GB' storage rate; medium confidence because of this unit ambiguity. A pricier alternative exists for faster restores if the snapshot is instead stored on Premium/SSD-class storage ($0.132/GB per month, LRS, confirmed live at the same 'us-east' region setting) -- not recorded, since a cost-minimizing customer retaining snapshot capacity would use the cheaper Standard-storage option.

Volumes Block Storage, live pricing page: '100 GiB $0.015 [/hour] $10.00 [/month]', '500 GiB $0.074 $50.00', '1,000 GiB $0.149 $100.00' -- all three points confirm a flat $0.10/GiB-month; unit stated explicitly as GiB, no conversion needed. No region selector on this page; it states pricing is flat across all data centers: 'Always know what you'll pay with monthly caps and flat pricing across all data centers.' IOPS/throughput are not mentioned anywhere on the pricing page; it cannot be determined whether performance is bundled into this rate or simply undisclosed, so no baseline is named for this row. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: DigitalOcean sells exactly one volume type, 'Volumes Block Storage' -- confirmed live, the page names no other volume SKU or tier.

Volumes Snapshot, live pricing page: 'Volumes Snapshot $0.06/GiB per month'. Unit stated explicitly as GiB, no conversion needed. The page does not state whether snapshots are full copies or incremental deltas -- recorded as published, without assuming either.
